A photograph for the neighbour

Shared bank: because | for | good | kitten | much | one | quiet | to | visit | we

On Sunday, my sister and I ____1____ our neighbour, Mrs Bell. Her cat had three new ____2____, and she wanted a photograph to send to her son. We took our camera and a clean blanket. Mrs Bell asked us to keep ____3____ voices low so the animals would stay calm.

At first, the smallest kitten hid under a chair. My sister waited ____4____ instead of reaching for it. Soon it came out and sat beside the others. I took my ____5____ picture, but my finger covered part of the lens. I tried again after checking how I held the camera.

The next photograph was much ____6____. All the kittens appeared in it, and the window gave enough light. Mrs Bell asked us ____7____ choose one copy for her. We looked at the pictures together rather than picking only our own favourites. In one, the mother cat was washing a kitten's ear. That was the photograph she liked ____8____.

We put the camera away ____9____ the kittens needed a rest. Mrs Bell made tea for us and told us about her son's two cats. Before leaving, we wrote the date on the back of the printed photograph. She thanked us ____10____ our help. I had expected a quick job, but the slow part had given us time to notice the animals and hear her stories. We went home with no special picture for ourselves, but with an invitation to visit again.

The bread at the wrong door

Shared bank: but | careful | easy | heavy | make | read | they | two | we | wrong

Yesterday, our class ____1____ rolls for the school breakfast club. A teacher checked every bag before we carried it across the playground. Each bag had a label, but two classroom numbers looked almost the same in the rain. We carried one bag to the ____2____ room and returned to find its pupils already eating.

The teacher asked us to check the labels ____3____. Room16 should have received the smaller bag; Room18 needed the larger one. We had switched ____4____. Fortunately, no one had opened the second bag. An adult helped us exchange it before breakfast began there. We did not take food away from anyone who had already been served.

This was our ____5____ delivery morning, so we were still learning the route. The first had gone smoothly, which may have made us too confident. Today the bags were also ____6____ than before because the club had more visitors. We asked for a trolley rather than struggling across the wet ground.

Afterwards, we made new labels with larger numbers. We placed them where the teacher could see them ____7____. The teacher suggested ____8____ the room number aloud at each door. One person would read while another checked the list. We tried the arrangement on the empty return journey. It took a little longer, ____9____ everyone agreed it was worth doing. The pupils thanked ____10____ for bringing the breakfast. I was glad the mistake had become a small problem to solve, not a secret that might leave another group waiting.

We needed to replace it in every classroom that had received the earlier version. Simply telling our own class would leave the same confusion ____4____.

The monitor helped prepare a short correction. It named the affected event and gave the new time ____5____. It also said that normal lessons before the assembly would continue as planned. That extra sentence mattered: some pupils had assumed the whole morning was changing. A useful correction had to explain both the change and its ____6____.

An adult checked the notice before it was shared. The old wall copies were removed, and teachers read the update aloud. By Friday, everyone in our class knew when to arrive. The speaker thanked the school for ____7____ with the delay. The monitor did not claim to have prevented every possible misunderstanding; she had helped solve one identifiable problem.

Afterwards, our teacher asked us to think about information we displayed. A date alone might not tell readers whether a notice was still current. We added a space for the ____8____ of each update and the name of the staff member who approved it. This would make later checks ____9____, though it could not replace checking itself. The best lesson was a practical one: when two records disagree, preserve the question long enough to find the right ____10____ rather than spreading whichever answer feels convenient.

Soon we had a short piece with a beginning, a quiet middle and a loud ending. We decided ____7____ play it once for the class next door.
